prompt.context: You are part of a consulting team working for a pharmaceutical manufacturer. The client has asked you to look at their current R&D portfolio and assess whether they are maximizing their potential with their current projects.
prompt.question: (1) How can you help them decide what information you would need? (2) What components do you think would round out a portfolio for this company?

clarifying_info.q: What is the current R&D expenditure annually?
clarifying_info.a: $1M annually, though calculations can be done using percentages only.

clarifying_info.q: Are there staffing concerns or expected layoffs/hiring changes?
clarifying_info.a: Current staffing needs are at equilibrium; layoffs and hiring are not expected to be necessary.

framework: Revenues and Expenses — assess financial capacity to fund R&D
Regulatory Environment — understand approval timelines and compliance requirements
Internal Issues — evaluate current pipeline, stage of projects, and resource allocation

Portfolio Mix Dimensions — analyze projects across multiple axes: new vs. existing business, new vs. current technologies, short vs. long duration, high vs. low investment, spread across business units, large vs. small projects

questions.prompt: What categories/dimensions should the company consider when structuring its R&D portfolio?
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm multiple axes of portfolio diversification. Strong answers name at least 4-5 distinct categories and explain why each matters for risk/return balance. The goal is to avoid over-concentration in any single dimension.

questions.prompt: Pick two of the categories you identified and create a 2x2 diagram. How would you suggest breaking up the expenditure across the four quadrants?
questions.guidance: Candidate should assign percentage allocations to each axis such that each axis sums to 100% and all four quadrant percentages sum to 100%. The key constraint: each row percentage x column percentage = quadrant percentage. Easy prompt acceptable if candidate has trouble with the math.

math.setup: Use Duration (Long 40% / Short 60%) and Dollar Investment (High 40% / Low 60%) as example axes. Each cell = row% x column%.
math.answer: The four quadrants sum to 100%. Each axis allocation is self-consistent (High+Low=100%, Long+Short=100%). The exact splits can vary as long as these constraints hold.

brainstorming.prompt: What components/categories should round out the R&D portfolio for this pharmaceutical company?

categories.name: Project Stage / Business Type
ideas: New business development vs. incremental improvements to existing products

categories.name: Technology Dimension
ideas: Investment in new/emerging technologies vs. current established technologies
Platform technologies with broad application vs. single-indication compounds

categories.name: Financial Dimension
ideas: High dollar investment projects vs. low dollar investment projects
Short payback period projects vs. long payback period projects

categories.name: Business Unit Spread
ideas: Spread of projects across different therapeutic areas or business units
Avoid over-concentration in one therapeutic area

categories.name: Project Size
ideas: Large flagship projects vs. small exploratory projects
Mix ensures some quick wins and some transformative bets

recommendation: The pharmaceutical company should structure its R&D portfolio across four key dimensions: (1) large vs. small investment, (2) long vs. short duration, (3) new business vs. existing business, and (4) spread across different business units.
This multi-dimensional balance maximizes expected return while reducing risk from over-concentration in any single area.
risks: Over-investing in long-duration high-cost projects creates near-term cash flow pressure
Insufficient diversity across business units creates concentration risk if one area faces regulatory setback
Too many small short-term projects may sacrifice transformative pipeline opportunities
next_steps: Map the current portfolio across the chosen 2x2 dimensions to identify gaps
Quantify the current allocation percentages vs. targets
Prioritize rebalancing actions based on strategic priorities and financial constraints
